subject: Environment
description: Covers Kaziranga, Gir, Manas, and Keibul Lamjao.

questions.stem: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is globally renowned for hosting the world's largest population of which endangered animal?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Kaziranga National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Assam. It is the undisputed global stronghold of the Greater One-Horned Rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis), hosting roughly two-thirds of the world's population. The park's vast expanse of tall elephant grass, marshland, and tropical moist broadleaf forests provides the perfect habitat.
DECOY BUSTING: The Asiatic Lion is found only in the Gir National Park (Gujarat). The Bengal Tiger is widespread but famously associated with Corbett, Ranthambore, and Sundarbans (though Kaziranga also has a very high tiger density). Snow Leopards are found in high-altitude Himalayan parks like Hemis (Ladakh).
EXAM INSIGHT: Kaziranga is crisscrossed by four main rivers, most notably the Brahmaputra. While it is famous for the rhino, it is also a Tiger Reserve and hosts significant populations of wild water buffalo and Asian elephants.

questions.stem: Which National Park in India is the ONLY natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in the wild?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, located in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, is the last and only remaining natural stronghold of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica). Once roaming freely from the Middle East to Eastern India, their population was decimated by hunting until conservation efforts in Gir saved them from extinction.
DECOY BUSTING: Kanha and Bandhavgarh (Madhya Pradesh) and Ranthambore (Rajasthan) are famous Tiger Reserves. Tigers and lions do not share any natural habitat in India today.
EXAM INSIGHT: Having the entire Asiatic lion population concentrated in one single forest is a massive conservation risk (a single epidemic like Canine Distemper Virus or a massive forest fire could wipe out the entire species). Hence, the Supreme Court has repeatedly ordered the relocation of some lions to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh to create a second home, though political resistance from Gujarat has delayed this.

questions.stem: Manas National Park, a UNESCO Natural World Heritage site, is located in which state?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Manas National Park is located in the Himalayan foothills in Assam. It is contiguous with the Royal Manas National Park in Bhutan. It is exceptionally diverse and holds multiple conservation titles: it is a National Park, a Tiger Reserve, an Elephant Reserve, and a Biosphere Reserve.
DECOY BUSTING: West Bengal hosts Jaldapara and Buxa. Arunachal has Namdapha. Sikkim has Khangchendzonga.
EXAM INSIGHT: Manas is famous for its rare and endemic wildlife, specifically the Assam Roofed Turtle, Hispid Hare, Golden Langur, and the Pygmy Hog. It was once placed on the "World Heritage in Danger" list due to heavy poaching and militancy (Bodo insurgency) but was successfully removed from the danger list in 2011 after recovery.

questions.stem: Keibul Lamjao National Park is famous for being the world's only floating national park. Which endangered deer species is exclusively found here?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Keibul Lamjao National Park is located on the Loktak Lake in Manipur. It is an integral part of the lake, composed of floating decomposed plant materials called 'phumdis'. It is the last and only natural habitat of the endangered Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii), also known as the brow-antlered deer or "dancing deer" (because it appears to dance as it walks on the unstable, bobbing phumdis).
DECOY BUSTING: Hangul is found exclusively in Dachigam National Park (Kashmir). Barasingha is famously the state animal of Madhya Pradesh (Kanha NP) and UP (Dudhwa NP). Chinkara is an antelope found in arid regions like Rajasthan.
EXAM INSIGHT: The Sangai is the state animal of Manipur. The construction of the Ithai Barrage has maintained high water levels year-round, preventing the phumdis from touching the lake bed during the dry season to absorb nutrients, thereby threatening the entire ecosystem.
